newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares close lower on Christmas Eve.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares close lower on Christmas Eve.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed lower on Tuesday as investors trimmed their positions and moved to the sidelines ahead of the Christmas holiday, brokers said.
The B share index fell 3.86 points or 2.90 percent to 129.38 on volume of 44.90 million shares worth HK$199.57 million compared with Monday's HK$194.31 million.
A spokesman for the Shenzhen Stock Exchange said there will be no trading on the city's B share market on Wednesday and Thursday due to the Christmas holiday. Trading will resume on Friday, he said.

"Investors reduced their holdings ahead of the holiday, which pushed down the index," an analyst said. December 25 and 26 are not public holidays in China but many foreign buyers of B shares are taking a holiday.
The fall was also due to profit-taking after a strong rebound on Monday, brokers said.
The A share market tumbled on Tuesday on a sell-off triggered by rumours that Beijing is drafting new measures to reduce speculation in the A share market, brokers said.
The A index dived 23.43 points or 7.27 percent to 298.82 on turnover of 4.67 billion yuan against 5.12 billion on Monday.
On the B share market, selling focused on cheap issues, brokers said.

Conglomerate Zhonghao tumbled HK$0.35 or 9.09 percent to HK$3.50 on volume of 399,100 shares. Television maker Huafa fell HK$0.30 or 8.36 percent to HK$3.29 on trade of 266,600 shares and Jiangling Motors fell HK$0.24 or 8.08 percent to HK$2.73, with 1.02 million shares changing hands.

Changan Automobile traded the most on volume of 6.65 million shares and closed down HK$0.09 at HK$4.01. Appliance maker Tsann Kuen bucked the trend and rose HK$0.07 to HK$3.43 on institutional buying, brokers said.
